piezas.titulo: Reading words: Transport and getting around
texto: Reading and spelling of transport signs: the word «รถ» (vehicle) has the initial consonant ร and the final consonant ถ (high class), which at the end of a syllable sounds like the voiceless alveolar stop [t] (rule แม่กด) with a high tone. «รถเมล์» has the silent consonant ล์ with the thantakhat sign. «สถานี» has the high-class consonant ส with the implicit short vowel a, ถ with the long vowel า (rising tone) and น with the vowel ี. «เปลี่ยน» has the consonant cluster pl (ปล) with the diphthong ื...ย and the mark ่ (low tone).

pregunta.texto: In the word «รถ» (vehicle / car), how does the final consonant ถ sound at the end of a syllable?

opciones.texto: As a voiceless alveolar stop [t] (แม่กด group)
opciones.explicacion: Correct: dental and alveolar consonants such as ถ sound like [t] at the end of a syllable.
Incorrect: aspiration does not occur in final position in Thai.
Incorrect: ถ does not belong to the liquid or nasal class.
